simple.meaning: כָּנַשׁ (kânash) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to assemble.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 3:2. The surrounding contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כָּנַשׁ (H3673) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: כָּנַשׁ (kânash) / H3673 is traced through Daniel 3:2, Daniel 3:3, Daniel 3:27 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H3673. kenash [ כְּנַשׁ ] verb gather ( ᵑ7 id. ; Old Aramaic Palmyrene בנש Lzb 298 ; Syriac ; see also Biblical Hebrew [ כָּנַס ); — Pe`al Infinitive , לְמִכְנַשׁ , followed by ל accusative of person Dan 3:2 . Hithpa. Participle plural מִתְכַּנְּשִׁין (were) assembled Dan 3:3 , 27 .

occurrences.englishText: Then Nebuchadnezzar the king sent to gather together the local governors, the deputies, and the governors, the judges, the treasurers, the counselors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the image which Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up.

Then the local governors, the deputies, and the governors, the judges, the treasurers, the counselors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces, were gathered together to the dedication of the image that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up; and they stood before the image that Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

The local governors, the deputies, and the governors, and the king’s counselors, being gathered together, saw these men, that the fire had no power on their bodies. The hair of their head wasn’t singed. Their pants weren’t changed, the smell of fire wasn’t even on them.
